Can't get up for school? Everyone says you're lazy. Except, it's your body clock.
In teens, the sleep hormone melatonin kicks in later at night.
So most teens aren't sleepy until after ten thirty, but you still need eight to ten hours.

text: So what if school started at ten A M?

A school in England tried it, with two thousand teens.
Absences from illness dropped by more than half.

text: And twelve percent more students made good progress.
Then the school switched back. And illness absences went up again.

The catch? You'd finish school later too.

text: Ten A M school. Better grades or total chaos? Comment one word.
